summary_paragraph: A male patient with hypogammaglobulinemia, mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and orthostatic hypotension was admitted for scheduled inpatient IVIG infusion. He received premedication with IV fluids and Benadryl, and the infusion was administered slowly overnight due to his fluid sensitivity. During the infusion, he experienced mild chest discomfort and shortness of breath, which resolved with oxygen and rate reduction. He remained on telemetry and was observed overnight. The following day, he reported residual grogginess but improved mental clarity by afternoon. He was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments, including a switch to chewable aspirin, and plans for potential transition to outpatient IVIG. No acute complications occurred.
